base_prompt: A shop offers a ten-percent discount on an item and then adds ten percent to the reduced price. Explain why the result is not the original price, using an item priced at 100 units. Keep your response near 80 words.
text: An item priced at 100 units receives a ten-percent discount, reducing its price by 10 units to 90 units. The subsequent ten-percent increase is calculated from this reduced price, not from the original price. Ten percent of 90 is 9, so adding it raises the price to 99 units. The result is therefore 1 unit less than the original price. The percentages are equal, but their monetary amounts differ because they are applied to different starting values.
